So two armies from these cities followed Tarun to recover his crown and chastised the Romans. When they had entered Roman territory, the consoles advanced against them. Val Valyrias with the infant infantry and Fallon's information formation. Brutus reconed in advance with the cavalry. Similarly, the enemy's calvary was in front of his main body, Areronus Tarkin, the king's son in command. The king himself followed with the legionnaires. Whilst still at a distance, Aaron distinguished the console by his escort of lictors as they drew nearer.

He clearly recognized Brutus by his features and in a transport of rage exclaimed, "That is the man who drove us from our country. See him proudly advancing adorned with our insignia. Ye God, Avengers of kings, aid me." With these words he dug spurs into his horse and rode straight at the console. Brutus saw that he was making for him. It was a point of honor in those days for the leaders to engage in single combat. So he eagerly accepted the challenge and they charged with such fury, neither of them thinking of protecting himself. If only he could wound his foe; that each drove his spear at the same moment through the other's shield and they fell dying from their horses with their spears sticking in them.

Prudence is traumatized by the execution of his two sons. There is now a void in his heart. There is now a tear in his heart. Right? But this tear is unleashing all this energy that he can now use against his enemy. Okay, that is a secret. Trauma is a drug. The Roman ways use trauma as a drug to empower you against your enemies.

The problem though is that the Roman army is much smaller than the king's army. So Romans are forced back into their city and hide behind their walls, under siege. There's a Roman nobleman named Mousius who decides to offer a proposal to the Senate. He says to the Senate, "Listen, we're never going to beat this king's army. What I can do is sneak into his camp and assassinate the king."

The Senate agrees. So Mousius swims across the Tyber and sneaks into an enemy camp. It's payday there—two men, the king and secretary, giving out cash to soldiers who look and dress the same. Mousius doesn't know which is which. At this point, he should come back another day and figure it out. But now he thinks it's 50/50. So he takes his dagger and stabs one of them—turns out to be the secretary. He's arrested and appears before the king.

The king says, "You tell me the truth or I will burn you in this fire." Mousius says, "Okay, the truth is this: I am one of hundreds of young Roman men who have sworn to come and kill you. One of us will succeed. I failed today, but tomorrow someone else will come. If you fail, someone else will come as well."

The king asks, "Are you telling the truth? If you are not telling the truth, I will burn you alive." Mousius takes his hand and puts it in a fire burning on the spot. The king is freaked out and says, "You Romans are the craziest bastards. You guys are demonic. I'm out of here."

Hence alone, he seeks help in utmost peril. He says, "I am a citizen of Rome. Men call me Mucus." As an enemy, he wishes to kill an enemy and has as much courage to meet death as he had to inflict it. It is the Roman nature to act bravely and suffer bravely.

I'm not alone in having made this resolve against you. Behind me there is a long list of those who aspire to the same distinction. If then it is your pleasure, make up your mind for a struggle in which you will every hour have to fight for your life and find an armed foe on the threshold of your royal tent. This is the war which we, the youth of Rome, declared against you.

We have no sir ranks, no pitched battle to fear. The matter will be settled between you alone and each one of us singly. The king, furious with anger and at the same time terrified at the unknown danger threatened that if he did not promptly explain the nature of the plot which he was darkly hinting at, he should be roasted alive.

Oo Mucus cried and learned how lightly those regard their bodies who have some great glory in view. Then he plunged his right hand into a fire burning on the spot, showing the king that courage is more than just a show.
